name: Flex
description: A flex container primitive with direction, gap, alignment and distribution props; defaults to a horizontal row.

anatomy.description: A display-flex root; direction defaults to row.
row, row-reverse, column or column-reverse along the main axis.
align and justify map to align-items and justify-content.
Lets rows flow onto multiple lines when space runs out.

dos: Use justify="between" for label-plus-action toolbar rows.
Enable wrap for tag rows and button groups that must survive narrow widths.
Use the as prop when the grouping has semantics, such as nav or a list.
donts: Don't use Flex for a plain evenly spaced stack; Stack is the more specific choice.
Don't reverse the direction when that would make visual order contradict the DOM reading order.
Don't duplicate the gap with margins on children.

examples.title: Row with distribution
examples.description: Children spread across the row with wrapping enabled, the common toolbar and tag-row shape.

examples.title: Column direction
examples.description: The same container stacks children vertically with consistent gaps and start alignment.

guidance.useWhen: Children need one-dimensional arrangement with control over direction, wrapping, alignment and distribution.
guidance.avoidWhen: You only need an evenly spaced vertical or horizontal stack; Stack is the simpler, more specific choice.
guidance.behavior: Flex maps props to flexbox values and merges any caller className and style, so one-off overrides stay possible.
guidance.responsive: Wrap lets rows collapse onto multiple lines; pair with responsive classes when direction itself must change per breakpoint.

notes: Flex is purely visual; use the as prop for a semantic element (nav, list) when the grouping has meaning.
Reverse directions change only visual order, so keep the DOM order matching the reading order.
